about: Every vulnerability, bug and breach found on videos.promptugal.news, published (Dinis Cruz, 18 November 2026, about 15:15 UTC). A fixed finding in full; an open one as its title, severity and state only, until it is fixed. Never deleted.

findings.title: Open findings would have been published in full in the JSON
findings.found_by: AppSec post-review (a Sonnet sub-agent of videos.b@PrompTugal.dinis), before the first push
findings.detail: The page showed an open finding by title, severity and state only, but the JSON copy was written raw, with its detail and fix. Latent: no finding existed yet. Never published.
findings.fix: The JSON now carries only id, title, severity, state and date for any finding not fixed.

findings.title: A crafted URL could add a link in the markdown twins
findings.found_by: AppSec post-review (a Sonnet sub-agent of videos.b@PrompTugal.dinis), before the first push
findings.detail: An https URL holding ") [text](" passed the https check and was written raw into the markdown twins, where it would end the link and start another. Never published: no such URL is in the data.
findings.fix: URLs in markdown are normalised and ( ) [ ] < > quotes, spaces, backslashes, backticks and bars are percent-encoded; bare URLs are wrapped in angle brackets.

findings.title: A title with line breaks could add lines to llms.txt and the twins
findings.found_by: AppSec post-review (a Sonnet sub-agent of videos.b@PrompTugal.dinis), before the first push
findings.detail: Line breaks in a title or channel name survived into the markdown twins and llms.txt, which language models read: a way to slip text that looks like an instruction onto its own line. Never published.
findings.fix: Every field is reduced to one line: control characters removed, whitespace collapsed.

findings.title: Some direction marks and zero-width characters were not removed
findings.found_by: AppSec post-review (a Sonnet sub-agent of videos.b@PrompTugal.dinis), before the first push
findings.detail: U+200E, U+200F, U+061C, zero-width characters and U+FEFF passed through; they can make text read differently from what it holds. The Arabic title carried a right-to-left mark.
findings.fix: Removed with the other control and direction-override characters.

findings.title: The place name was not escaped in a video's markdown twin
findings.found_by: AppSec post-review (a Sonnet sub-agent of videos.b@PrompTugal.dinis), before the first push
findings.detail: The place was written raw into the twin's "Where" line. Never exploitable with the data as it is (one fixed place).
findings.fix: Escaped as the other fields.

findings.title: The threat model claimed more than the code did
findings.found_by: AppSec post-review (a Sonnet sub-agent of videos.b@PrompTugal.dinis), before the first push
findings.detail: It said the twins escape markdown and that bidi characters are removed; findings 2 to 5 made that partly untrue.
findings.fix: Updated after the fixes.

findings.title: The embedded video was not tied to the source link
findings.found_by: AppSec post-review (a Sonnet sub-agent of videos.b@PrompTugal.dinis), before the first push
findings.detail: A record could embed one YouTube id while its source link pointed to another video.
findings.fix: The build stops unless the source URL's v= is the embedded id.

findings.title: The API would publish any extra field in the data
findings.found_by: AppSec post-review (a Sonnet sub-agent of videos.b@PrompTugal.dinis), before the first push
findings.detail: Each video's JSON was its record spread whole, so a field added by mistake (a private note) would be published.
findings.fix: The API publishes only a fixed list of fields.

findings.title: Four channels to confirm as organisations, not private people
findings.found_by: AppSec post-review (a Sonnet sub-agent of videos.b@PrompTugal.dinis), before the first push
findings.detail: The reviewer could not confirm that SECTIES PB, The Spotlight: Beyond Profession, VOICE OF NEPAL TV - VON and RVTV are organisations rather than private people.
findings.fix: Accepted under Dinis's line of 18 November 2026 (~15:35 UTC, Website board/guidance/2026-11-18-people-blogs-cyber-and-simulated-payments.md): anyone who publishes in public is named and linked by the name they published under; never private information or a personal contact; take-down on request. Each channel is shown by its published name only.

findings.title: No frame-ancestors protection
findings.found_by: AppSec post-review (a Sonnet sub-agent of videos.b@PrompTugal.dinis), before the first push
findings.detail: A Content Security Policy in a meta tag cannot set frame-ancestors, and GitHub Pages cannot send headers, so another site could frame these pages.
findings.fix: Accepted: the pages hold no forms, sign-in or actions to trick a reader into.

findings.title: A URL given as a list passed the https check
findings.found_by: AppSec post-review (a Sonnet sub-agent of videos.b@PrompTugal.dinis), before the push
findings.detail: new URL() turns its argument into a string, so a one-item list holding an https address passed the check; the HTML escaped it, but the JSON would have carried a list where a string belongs. Never published.
findings.fix: The URL checks accept strings only.

findings.title: The size cap was checked only after the whole answer was read
findings.found_by: AppSec post-review (a Sonnet sub-agent of videos.b@PrompTugal.dinis), before the push
findings.detail: The library's answer was read into memory in full before its size was compared with the 2 MB cap, so a compromised host could have sent far more within the timeout. Never happened: the answers so far are about 50 KB.
findings.fix: The bytes are counted as they arrive and the read stops at the cap.

findings.title: A failed read overwrote the record of the last good one
findings.found_by: AppSec post-review (a Sonnet sub-agent of videos.b@PrompTugal.dinis), before the push
findings.detail: A failure rewrote sync.json, so the site would have shown the failure's time as the last read and the next read would have kept a duplicate raw copy. Never happened.
findings.fix: A failure is written to sync-error.json; sync.json keeps describing the copy on disk.

findings.title: Impossible dates from the library were accepted
findings.found_by: AppSec post-review (a Sonnet sub-agent of videos.b@PrompTugal.dinis), before the push
findings.detail: A date was checked by its shape only, so 2026-99-99 would have shown as nonsense on a card. Never happened.
findings.fix: Only real calendar dates are taken; others are left out.

findings.title: Free text could pass as the last-read time
findings.found_by: AppSec post-review (a Sonnet sub-agent of videos.b@PrompTugal.dinis), before the push
findings.detail: The library sync record's time was checked only by whether a date could be parsed from it, so text around a date would have been published in the sources JSON as it was. Never happened.
findings.fix: Only an ISO time is taken, and it is normalised before it is shown or published.

findings.title: A link among the kept reads would have been followed
findings.found_by: AppSec post-review (a Sonnet sub-agent of videos.b@PrompTugal.dinis), before the push
findings.detail: A symbolic link with a kept-read name would have been read and its size and hash published. Needs write access to the repository; never happened.
findings.fix: Only regular files are read.

findings.title: A withdrawal could be undone by item order
findings.found_by: AppSec post-review (a Sonnet sub-agent of videos.b@PrompTugal.dinis), before the push
findings.detail: If the library listed a withdrawn item before a held one for the same YouTube video, the held one would have been added. Never happened.
findings.fix: Every YouTube id the library holds as anything but held is withdrawn, whatever the order.

findings.title: Raw status text reached the build log
findings.found_by: AppSec post-review (a Sonnet sub-agent of videos.b@PrompTugal.dinis), before the push
findings.detail: A status holding line breaks or terminal escape codes would have reached the CI log as it was. Never happened.
findings.fix: Only letters and hyphens of a status are logged.

findings.title: The validator's image checks could be stepped around
findings.detail: The new image checks read only lower-case img tags with a double-quoted src, did not look at srcset, picture, source or url() in stylesheets, and counted one credit per page rather than per image. The CSP still allowed only this site and i.ytimg.com, so nothing outside could load. Never happened.
findings.fix: Any img tag in any case; a missing, unquoted or single-quoted src fails; srcset, picture and source fail; url() in a stylesheet fails; one credit per YouTube image; the old claim that the page asks nothing of YouTube before play fails in its usual wordings.
findings.found_by: AppSec post-review (a Sonnet sub-agent of videos.b@PrompTugal.dinis), before the push

findings.title: REALITY.md still said nothing is requested from YouTube before play
findings.detail: After the preview images, line 15 contradicted the new entry and the site.
findings.fix: Line 15 now says the preview image loads from i.ytimg.com on page open and the video on play.
findings.found_by: AppSec post-review (a Sonnet sub-agent of videos.b@PrompTugal.dinis), before the push

findings.title: The embeds threat model did not list the image host it now trusts
findings.detail: 'Trusts ... Nothing else' left out i.ytimg.com.
findings.fix: The trust line names i.ytimg.com, for images only.
findings.found_by: AppSec post-review (a Sonnet sub-agent of videos.b@PrompTugal.dinis), before the push

findings.title: The sites bar's pin was checked only against our own copy
findings.detail: A change editing both the vendored bar files and the stored pin in data/sites/latest.json would have passed the build, the validator and the leak scan; only the wake-time sync compared with the live registry. Never happened.
findings.fix: release.sh now runs scripts/sync-sites.mjs --check before every push: our vendored files against the live registry's pin, failing closed if it cannot confirm them.
findings.found_by: AppSec post-review (a Sonnet sub-agent of videos.b@PrompTugal.dinis), before the push

findings.title: The leak scan's pin exemption was wider than the pins
findings.detail: Any version key and any sha256, sha384 or sha512 value of 43 to 86 characters under js, css or render was exempt, so a secret dressed as such a value could have hidden there. Never happened.
findings.fix: Exempt only bar.versions[bar.ours].integrity with exactly the keys js, css and render, each exactly sha256-<43>=, and each equal to the fingerprint of our own vendored file of that version; ten tests.
findings.found_by: AppSec post-review (a Sonnet sub-agent of videos.b@PrompTugal.dinis), before the push

findings.title: The served bar files were not the checked bytes
findings.detail: The build checked the vendored files but served the copy of src/ made before the check, and the validator never hashed what is served. Never happened.
findings.fix: The build writes the checked bytes into _site; the validator hashes the served files against the stored pin, requires version 1.2.1, and checks every link in the bar is https *.promptugal.news.
findings.found_by: AppSec post-review (a Sonnet sub-agent of videos.b@PrompTugal.dinis), before the push

findings.title: The build skipped some of the sync's checks on the sites
findings.detail: The build did not repeat the checks for duplicate ids or hosts and for promptugal.news first. Not exploitable: the CSP still only held *.promptugal.news hosts.
findings.fix: One shared siteHosts() check, used by the sync and the build.
findings.found_by: AppSec post-review (a Sonnet sub-agent of videos.b@PrompTugal.dinis), before the push

findings.title: Small gaps in the sync script and the checks
findings.detail: A stale sync-error.json stayed after a later success; the temporary file had a fixed name; the stored read time was logged as written; the preview and stylesheet checks missed the /on...= and image-set() forms; the embeds threat model said images came only from i.ytimg.com.
findings.fix: Cleared on success; a temporary name per process; the read time logged only in its exact shape; both forms now fail; the threat models updated.
findings.found_by: AppSec post-review (a Sonnet sub-agent of videos.b@PrompTugal.dinis), before the push
